scenario: AITA for lying to my bf and letting him believe his ex cheated on him? | I know this sounds really bad but just hear me out. it's been eating me up inside so I'd like some feedback. We're currently college seniors and we started dating only 4 months ago. For his first two years he was dating another girl that I somewhat knew since we're in the same sorority but I wasn't close to. I had a crush on him since basically freshman year but I knew he was dating this girl. Anyways they ultimately broke up because he suspected she was cheating due to rumors about a party where she reportedly danced and kissed some guy. I was also there but I don't remember seeing her since it was a huge venue that was hosted by our sorority and we didn't really have overlapping friends circles. So when we started dating he was obviously still really torn up about his ex and questioning their break-up. It really stung to see him still so torn up about it, since all I wanted for us was a new start and for him to forget his ex completely. So when he asked me if I had seen his ex at that party, I don't know why but I lied and said that I had seen her with other guys. That really sealed it for him and I think he's moved on a lot faster. He says it's a no-brainer that they broke up because she cheated and now he knows for sure. He says he feels a lot better knowing that he didn't dump her for no reason. I know there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. He's so much happier than before and he has no regrets about his exgf anymore. So, am I the asshole for lying and keeping up with the lie?

First, the situation: They've been dating for four months, and he's a college senior. He was previously dating another girl for two years, and they broke up because he suspected she was cheating. The woman in question had a crush on him since freshman year but knew he was in a relationship. When they started dating, he was still emotionally torn about the breakup. She didn't want him to be stuck in the past, so when he asked her if she saw his ex at a party, she lied and said she saw her with other guys. This made him feel more confident that his ex cheated, and he's happier now without any regrets. Now, I need to consider whether lying in this situation is right or wrong. On one hand, she wanted to help him move on and be happy. On the other hand, lying can damage trust in a relationship, which is really important. I think about the consequences of her lie. He's happier now, which is a positive outcome. But if he ever found out she lied, it could hurt him deeply. Trust is a big deal, and once broken, it's hard to rebuild. Also, she's keeping the lie alive, which means she's continuing to deceive him. That's not good for their relationship in the long run. Another angle is the intent behind the lie. She didn't want him to be miserable and wanted a fresh start. Her intentions were good, but the method was wrong. There are other ways to help someone move on without lying. For example, she could have encouraged him to focus on their relationship or helped him process his emotions in a healthy way. I also consider the impact on her. Lying can cause internal conflict and stress, as she's keeping a secret. This might affect her mental health and the relationship's dynamics. In conclusion, while her intentions were to make him happy, lying is not the right approach. It undermines trust and can lead to bigger issues down the line. There are healthier ways to support someone through a breakup without resorting to deception.
